title: Pauli operators
summary: The single-qubit matrices I, X (bit flip), Y and Z (phase flip). Strings of them describe errors and checks on many qubits; two strings commute or anticommute.

title: Clifford gates
summary: Gates that map Pauli strings to Pauli strings under conjugation, generated by H, S and CNOT. They are efficiently simulable and cheap on a surface-code processor; T is not Clifford.

title: Stabilizers
summary: Commuting Pauli strings that leave every code state unchanged. Measuring them reveals errors without disturbing encoded information.

title: Syndromes and detection events
summary: The measured stabilizer outcomes as bits. Errors flip the bits of the stabilizers they anticommute with; under repeated rounds, decoders use the changes, called detection events.

title: Code distance
summary: The fewest single-qubit errors that change the logical state undetected. A distance-d code corrects floor((d-1)/2) errors.

title: Logical qubits
summary: One qubit of information stored across many physical qubits by a code, acted on by logical operators that commute with every stabilizer.

title: The T gate
summary: T = diag(1, e^{iπ/4}). It is not Clifford, makes the gate set universal with the Cliffords, and on a surface code each T consumes a magic state, so estimates count T gates.

title: Magic states
summary: Resource states that, consumed with Clifford operations and measurement, apply a non-Clifford gate. Factories distil them; their supply rate can limit fault-tolerant runtime.
